title: Graph BFS: Minimum Steps
contract: Return shortest edge distance from source to target in an undirected unweighted graph; −1 means unreachable.
signature: int solve(int n,int[][] edges,int source,int target)
brute: int[][] d=new int[n][n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++){Arrays.fill(d[i],1000000);d[i][i]=0;}for(int[] e:edges){d[e[0]][e[1]]=1;d[e[1]][e[0]]=1;}for(int k=0;k<n;k++){for(int i=0;i<n;i++)for(int j=0;j<n;j++)d[i][j]=Math.min(d[i][j],d[i][k]+d[k][j]);emit("Compute all-pairs distances","via",k,"source distances",d[source]);}return d[source][target]>=1000000?-1:d[source][target];
optimal: List<List<Integer>> g=graph(n,edges);int[] d=new int[n];Arrays.fill(d,-1);d[source]=0;Deque<Integer> q=new ArrayDeque<>();q.add(source);while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();emit("Visit in increasing distance order","vertex",u,"distance",d,"queue",q);if(u==target)return d[u];for(int v:g.get(u))if(d[v]<0){d[v]=d[u]+1;q.add(v);}}return -1;
reasoning: All-pairs dynamic programming is a correct but expensive baseline for a single unweighted query.
BFS enqueues vertices by increasing distance, so the first discovery of a vertex is a shortest path.
Set distance before enqueueing. DFS does not promise minimum edges; weighted edges require a different relaxation order.
